title: Algebra and Linear Equations
subtitle: Solve equations carefully, respect restrictions, and interpret linear functions as rates and initial values.

isi.content: An equation is a statement that two expressions have the same value. It stays true when the same operation is performed on both sides. The goal is to isolate the variable without changing the solution set.

items: Simplify each side of the equation.
Collect variable terms on one side.
Collect constant terms on the other side.
Divide or multiply to isolate the variable.
Check the solution in the original equation.

isi.content: Write one algebraic step per line. This makes sign errors easier to find and keeps both sides balanced.
Undo operations in reverse order. Addition is undone by subtraction, multiplication is undone by division, and so on.

isi.title: Example: one-step equation
isi.content: To solve \(x-1.5=6\), add 1.5 to both sides: \(x=7.5\).

isi.title: Example: multi-step equation
isi.content: For \(3x-2=5-0.5x\), add \(0.5x\) to both sides to get \(3.5x-2=5\). Add 2, then divide by 3.5: \(3.5x=7\), so \(x=2\).
If an equation has the same variable expression on both sides, move one copy of that expression first. Keep the sign attached to the term when it crosses the equals sign.
\[a(b+c)=ab+ac\]
Use the distributive property before combining like terms. Like terms have the same variable part and exponent.

items.title: Cannot combine
items.content: \(3x+5\) cannot become \(8x\) because one term has a variable and the other is a constant.

items.title: Distribute
items.content: \(2(x+5)=2x+10\). Multiply 2 by every term inside the parentheses.

isi.content: For an equation with several fractions, multiply every term by the least common denominator. This removes the fractions while preserving equality.

isi.title: Example: clear fractions
isi.content: To solve \(\dfrac{2}{3}x-\dfrac{1}{6}=\dfrac{5}{2}\), multiply every term by 6: \(4x-1=15\). Then \(4x=16\), so \(x=4\).

isi.title: Example: a fractional expression
isi.content: For \(\dfrac{x-3}{2}=-3\), multiply both sides by 2: \(x-3=-6\). Therefore, \(x=-3\).
When decimals are terminating, multiplying by 10, 100, or 1,000 can make the equation easier to read.
A denominator can never equal zero. Write these restrictions before multiplying or cross-multiplying.

isi.title: Example: one denominator
isi.content: For \(\dfrac{6}{x}=4\), the restriction is \(x\ne0\). Multiplying by \(x\) gives \(6=4x\), so \(x=\dfrac32\), which satisfies the restriction.

isi.title: Example: cross-multiplication
isi.content: For \(\dfrac{2}{x}=\dfrac{8}{x+3}\), the restrictions are \(x\ne0\) and \(x\ne-3\). Cross-multiply: \(2(x+3)=8x\), so \(x=1\).
Cross-multiplication is valid only when the original denominators are nonzero. Always test the final value in the original equation.
To solve a radical equation, isolate the radical before squaring. Squaring can create an extraneous solution, so check every candidate in the original equation.

isi.title: Example: radical equation
isi.content: For \(\sqrt{4x}=12\), square both sides: \(4x=144\), so \(x=36\). Checking gives \(\sqrt{4(36)}=12\).

isi.title: Example: domain check
isi.content: For \(\sqrt{2x+6}+4=x+3\), isolate the radical to get \(\sqrt{2x+6}=x-1\). Since a square root is nonnegative, \(x\ge1\) is required before squaring.
When \(x^2=9\), the solutions are \(x=3\) and \(x=-3\). A squared equation usually has two solutions unless a restriction removes one.
\[y=mx+b\]

items.title: Slope \(m\)
items.content: The rate of change: how much \(y\) changes for each 1-unit increase in \(x\).

items.title: Intercept \(b\)
items.content: The initial value, or the value of \(y\) when \(x=0\).

items.title: Function value
items.content: The output found by substituting an input into the model.

isi.title: Example: commission model
isi.content: Julia earns a base pay of USD \(2\) per hour and USD \(3\) for each item sold. If \(x\) is the number of items and \(y\) is the total revenue, then \(y=2+3x\). The intercept is 2 and the rate is 3.
The units of the slope matter. In a cost model, slope may be dollars per mile; in a water-level model, it may be gallons per hour.
A linear model can describe a fixed starting amount plus a constant rate of change. A negative slope describes a quantity that decreases over time.

isi.title: Example: fixed fee and rate
isi.content: A car rental company charges USD \(50\) plus USD \(0.25\) per mile. For \(m\) miles, \(C(m)=50+0.25m\). At 80 miles, the cost is \(50+0.25(80)=70\) dollars.

isi.title: Example: decreasing value
isi.content: A car worth USD \(25{,}000\) loses USD \(2{,}000\) each year. Its value after \(t\) years is \(V(t)=25{,}000-2{,}000t\).

isi.title: Example: water level
isi.content: For \(L(t)=500-2t\), the tank starts with 500 gallons and loses 2 gallons per hour. It is empty when \(0=500-2t\), so \(t=250\) hours.

materi.judul: Solving from tables, graphs, and two points

isi.content: A constant first difference in a table indicates a linear relationship. The slope between two points is
After finding the slope, substitute a known point into \(y=mx+b\) to find the intercept.

isi.title: Example: two points
isi.content: A line passes through \((2,11)\) and \((8,35)\). Its slope is \(\dfrac{35-11}{8-2}=4\). Using \((2,11)\), \(11=4(2)+b\), so \(b=3\). The equation is \(y=4x+3\).
Check whether the slope has a meaningful unit and whether the intercept makes sense in the situation. Some models are only valid for a restricted domain, such as nonnegative time.

latihan.question: Find the value of \(x\): \(\dfrac{6}{x}=4\).
discussion: Divide by 4: \(x=\dfrac64=\dfrac32\), which satisfies the restriction.

latihan.question: Find all real values of \(x\): \(x^2=9\).
discussion: Taking the square root of both sides gives two possibilities: \(x=3\) or \(x=-3\).

latihan.question: Solve: \(\dfrac{2}{x}=\dfrac{8}{x+3}\).
discussion: The solution does not violate either restriction.

latihan.question: If \(\dfrac{x-1}{3}=k\) and \(k=3\), what is the value of \(x\)?
If \(\dfrac{a}{b}=2\), what is the value of \(\dfrac{4b}{a}\)?
If \(16+4x\) is 10 more than 14, what is the value of \(8x\)?
If \(3r=18\), what is the value of \(6r+3\)?
If \(\dfrac{7}{9}x-\dfrac{4}{9}x=\dfrac14+\dfrac5{12}\), what is the value of \(x\)?
discussion: Combine the right side using denominator 12: \(\dfrac14+\dfrac5{12}=\dfrac3{12}+\dfrac5{12}=\dfrac23\).

latihan.question: If \(\dfrac35w=\dfrac43\), what is the value of \(w\)?
discussion: Multiply both sides by \(\dfrac53\), the reciprocal of \(\dfrac35\).

latihan.question: A car rental company charges a flat fee of USD \(50\) plus USD \(0.25\) per mile driven. Which function gives the cost \(C\) for \(m\) miles?
discussion: The flat fee is the constant 50.

latihan.question: Maria currently has USD \(100\) and saves USD \(20\) every week. Write a linear function for her total savings \(S\) after \(w\) weeks.
discussion: The initial savings are 100, so the intercept is 100.
The savings increase by 20 dollars per week, so the slope is 20.

latihan.question: The function \(C(x)=15+0.10x\) gives the monthly cost of a phone plan, where \(x\) is the number of extra minutes. What is the total cost for 200 extra minutes?
discussion: Therefore, the total cost is USD 35, choice C.

latihan.question: The water level in a tank is modeled by \(L(t)=500-2t\), where \(t\) is hours. After how many hours will the tank be empty?

additionalPractice.question: What is the slope of \(y=4x-7\)?
discussion: The coefficient of \(x\) is 4, so the slope is 4, choice C.

additionalPractice.question: A taxi charges USD \(3\) plus USD \(2.50\) per mile. What is the cost of an 8-mile ride?
A line has slope \(-4\) and y-intercept 9. Write its equation.
Two plans have costs \(A(x)=35+2x\) and \(B(x)=11+5x\). For what value of \(x\) are the costs equal?
A quantity decreases linearly from 840 to 660 over 12 hours. Write a model \(Q(t)\) for the quantity after \(t\) hours.
discussion: The rate is \(-180\div12=-15\) units per hour.

additionalPractice.question: A line passes through \((2,11)\) and \((8,35)\). Find its equation.
Salim buys tennis-match tickets. The equation \(T=15n+12\) gives the total cost for \(n\) tickets. What does 12 represent?
options: The total amount paid for one ticket
The total amount paid for any number of tickets
discussion: In \(T=15n+12\), the coefficient 15 is the per-ticket cost.
The constant 12 is paid even when \(n=0\), so it represents the fixed service fee, choice B.

additionalPractice.question: Kathy repairs phones. The number left at the end of each day is modeled by \(P=108-23d\). What does 108 represent?
options: Kathy starts with 108 phones to fix
discussion: Therefore, 108 is the initial number of phones to fix. In the stated context, that is the starting amount represented by choice B.

additionalPractice.question: A pediatrician uses \(h=3a+28.6\) to estimate a boy's height. What is the estimated yearly increase?
discussion: Therefore, the model predicts an increase of 3 height units per year, choice A.

additionalPractice.question: At a restaurant, \(n\) cups of tea are made using \(t\) tea bags. If \(t=n+2\), how many additional tea bags are needed for each additional cup?
discussion: This means the number of tea bags increases by 1 for every additional cup, choice B.

additionalPractice.question: A graph of total boat-rental cost includes the points \((0,5),(1,8),(2,11),(3,14),(4,17),(5,20)\). Which equation represents the relationship?
discussion: The cost increases by 3 when the number of hours increases by 1, so the slope is 3.

additionalPractice.question: The average number of students per classroom is modeled by \(y=0.56x+27.2\). What does 0.56 represent?
options: The total number of students in 2000
The average students per classroom in 2000
The estimated yearly increase in average students per classroom
The difference between the 2010 and 2000 averages
discussion: The coefficient of \(x\) is the slope, or rate of change.
Thus, 0.56 represents the estimated yearly increase in the average number of students per classroom, choice C.
